U2's 44 warm rows are byte-identical repeats (same prompt re-sent; cached = 64*floor(L/64)), lengths 314-1550. U4's 372 warm rows are appends (every turn adds one body; rep=1, so no identical repeat exists anywhere in the 438 rows), prompts 934-12,393. Anchoring the grid law at the previous prompt instead of the current one does NOT rescue it either: cached == 64*floor((L_prev-1)/64) holds on only 18/39 control (none) rows and 62/216 pre-event rows - e.g. U4/append/none/u4-s1 turn 3 has L=2642, prev 1803 (law 1792) but measured 896 - so the reusable prefix lags the previous prompt as well. Both claims stand only when scoped: U2 = identical-repeat, U4 = append. Prompt size and hybrid attention are the same on both, so they are not the regime difference; the access pattern is.
